g.text: 1,000 random sets per size and null; the two nulls are the same 5,000
gene sets re-signed two ways. Points are 5 signatures x 2 weightings
at the primary tier (1 held back for incomplete mapping). Published
weights sit at percentiles 25.4 to 65.3 of the sign-randomised null
with external coefficients and 19.1 to 64.9 with weights signed in
TCGA-KIRC; outcome-signing itself induces the correlation, so that
null sits higher (15.9 to 30.9 and 8.6 to 36.7)

g.text: Random sets, 528 patients, 173 deaths; the sign-randomised
null has median HR 1.00 while the outcome-signed null's
sets are prognostic by construction (95% at p < 0.05).
Published weights sit at percentiles 99.8 to 100.0 of the
outcome-signed null with external coefficients and 99.7 to
+ age, sex, T, N, M1, ordinal
5 primary-tier signatures scored with their published gene sets (2 with coefficients published outside this
cohort and 3 whose per-gene weights had to be signed by a univariate Cox fit in this cohort), 520-528 patients,
172-173 deaths; 20 of 20 intervals exclude 1. Attenuation of the clinically adjusted log hazard ratio on adding
the three STAR metrics: -4.9 to -2.6 per cent with external coefficients and -19.0 to -11.1 with weights signed
in this cohort; on residualising the expression instead, -15.0 to -5.1 and -23.6 to -13.2
Published signatures under four specifications, by weight provenance

5 primary-tier signatures scored with their published gene sets (2 with coefficients published outside this
cohort and 3 whose per-gene weights had to be signed by a univariate Cox fit in this cohort), Spearman rho, n =
528; observed 0.172 to 0.434 with external coefficients and 0.114 to 0.428 with weights signed in TCGA-KIRC;
after residualisation every |rho| is below 0.04, which is the check that the adjustment does what it claims
